newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress party re-elects Kesri president.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress party re-elects Kesri president.

text.p: India's Congress Party on Thursday re-elected veteran politician Sitaram Kesri as its president with a overwhelming majority, it was officially announced.
"Sitaram Kesri has been elected president of the Congress Party," Chief Polling Officer Oscar Fernandes announced after day-long counting of votes.

He told reporters Kesri, 76, had won 6,224 of the 7,557 votes cast. Of his two younger rivals, Maharashtra strongman Sharad Pawar won 882 votes while Rajesh Pilot secured 354 votes. Ninety seven votes were found invalid.
Soon after his re-election Kesri said he would strive to fulfil the hopes and aspirations of party members who had put their faith in him and helped to achieve his resounding victory.
Jubilant Kesri supporters danced and waved slogans outside the Congress Party headquarters soon after his re-election became clear.

The voting for the politically influential post was held on Monday. It was only the third election in the 112-year history of India's oldest political party, traditionally dominated by charismatic leaders.

Once the driving force behind the movement against colonial rule, Congress has ruled India for all but five years since independence in 1947, with prime ministers Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi -- father, daughter and grandson -- in power for a total of 37 years.
Kesri swept aside the challenges of his two younger rivals who ran on a platform of rejuvenating the ailing party that was ejected from power last year.
